Lead paint: the short version for Oak Forest

Paint from before 1978 can contain lead, and 1970s housing is the normal case in Oak Forest. The practical effect is not that the work cannot be done. It is that it has to be contained and cleaned up to a standard, which is time at the start of a Oak Forest job and time at the end of it.

The rule does not say an Oak Forest house cannot be painted. It says how the area gets sealed off, how the dust is contained and how the site is left. The trigger in a 1975-median room is about six square feet of disturbed paint, twenty outside, and any window replacement or demolition at all.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Oak Forest.

62.4 percent of housing units were built before 1980, the nearest bucket to the 1978 line that the Census publishes, and that is the reading for Oak Forest. That puts most of the housing inside the federal lead-safe renovation rule, which attaches to pre-1978 homes and to work that disturbs the paint on them. In Illinois it is administered by EPA rather than by a state agency.

In Oak Forest it is worth asking about before the work starts rather than after the sanding has. Ask whoever you hire to say, in plain terms, how they intend to handle it at your particular address.

No lead-safe certification is claimed anywhere on this site, because no number has been provided to put here. The panel below leaves the slot open on purpose, in Oak Forest and everywhere else. Ask any contractor for theirs.
